questions.question: What is the basic syntax of Ruby?
questions.title: Ruby Syntax Basics
questions.direct_answer: Ruby is object-oriented and reads like prose: puts 'hello'; a = 10; a + 1. Comments: # (single line), =begin / =end (block). Strings: 'single' (no interpolation), "double #{x}" (interpolation). Symbols: :name. Variables: local (x), @instance, @@class, $global, UPPER (constant). Methods: def name; end. Classes: class Name; end. Blocks: { } or do/end. Conditionals: if/unless/case, each ending with end. Statements separated by newlines or semicolons (a = 1; b = 2). The keyword end closes blocks (no braces for methods/classes/conditionals). Punctuation matters: ? = predicate (empty?), ! = dangerous (sort!), = vs == vs ===. Semicolons optional. Ruby favors readability — name things clearly, avoid cleverness, use the idiomatic forms (each over while, map over manual loops).

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know the basic syntax: comments, strings, symbols, variable scopes, def/class/end, blocks, and end-closes-blocks.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Forgetting `end` (Ruby uses end, not braces, for methods/classes/conditionals), or mixing ' and " (interpolation only in double quotes).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Ruby syntax: # comments; 'single'/"double #{x}" strings; :symbol; x/@x/@@x/$x/UPPER vars; def/class end; {}/do-end blocks; ?/! naming; `end` closes blocks.

sections.title: Ruby syntax
sections.content:
```ruby
# Comments
puts 'hello'           # single-line comment
=begin
block comment
(=begin/=end must be at line start)
=end

# Strings and interpolation
'no interpolation'
"#{1 + 1}"             # '2' (interpolation in DOUBLE quotes)

# Symbols
:name                  # immutable, interned identifier

# Variables (scope by prefix)
x = 1                  # local
@count = 0             # instance
@@total = 0            # class
$global = 1            # global (avoid)
MAX = 100              # constant (UPPER)

# Methods and classes (end, not braces)
def greet(name); "Hi #{name}"; end
class User; end

# Blocks: { } (single) or do/end (multi)
[1,2].each { |x| puts x }
[1,2].each do |x|
  puts x
end

# Conditionals (end)
if x > 0; 'pos'; elsif x == 0; 'zero'; else; 'neg'; end
case x; when 1..5; 'small'; else 'big'; end

# Punctuation: ? predicate, ! dangerous, = vs == vs ===
arr.empty?             # ? -> bool
arr.sort!             # ! -> mutate in place
x == y                 # value equality

# Semicolons optional (newline-separated):
a = 1; b = 2          # same line
a = 1
b = 2                 # two lines
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Forgetting `end` — Ruby uses end for methods/classes/conditionals (no braces).
Mixing ' and " — interpolation only works in double quotes.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Methods/classes: def name; end / class Name; end (end, not braces).
Blocks: { } (single-line) or do...end (multi-line). Conditionals end with end.
? = predicate, ! = dangerous; = vs == vs ===; semicolons optional.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: Ruby is object-oriented and reads like prose: puts hello; a 10; a plus 1. Comments: hash (single line), begin end (block). Strings: single (no interpolation), double x (interpolation). Symbols: name. Variables: local (x), instance, class, global, UPPER (constant). Methods: def name; end. Classes: class Name; end. Blocks: braces or do end. Conditionals: if unless case, each ending with end. Statements separated by newlines or semicolons (a 1; b 2). The keyword end closes blocks (no braces for methods/classes/conditionals). Punctuation matters: ? equals predicate (empty), ! equals dangerous (sort), equals vs equals equals vs triple-equals. Semicolons optional. Ruby favors readability — name things clearly, avoid cleverness, use the idiomatic forms (each over while, map over manual loops). A common mistake is forgetting end, since Ruby uses end not braces, and mixing single and double quotes, since interpolation only works in double quotes.
